---
title: Group
description: "Labels that share learned latent groups."
---

`Group` learns shared groups for labels, such as merchants. Use it when you
want to test whether a learned grouping provides useful context for payment
prediction, as well as keeping a persistent merchant vocabulary.
[Category](category.qmd) is the simpler choice for independent label embeddings;
[Hash](hash.qmd) compares IDs without keeping a vocabulary.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model(
    preset="small",
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Group(
        n_groups=12,
    ),
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

One labeled payment:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
disputed: false
```

The groups identified need not match human categories.

## Input and options

Accepts scalar Boolean, integer, floating-point, string, or binary labels, with
one compatible Arrow family per field. Training grows the vocabulary;
validation, test, and prediction reuse it. Unknown labels remain `valued` and
use a shared unavailable assignment. Nulls have a separate state.

See [Online vocabulary](../concepts/online-vocabulary.qmd) for automatic growth,
admission timing with workers/DDP, supported training strategies, and changes
during fine-tuning.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `n_groups` | required | Integer `K` fixes the group count with 2 ≤ n_groups |
| `p_unavailable` | `0.01` | Training probability of replacing known input labels with unavailable content. Reconstruction answers remain intact. |

Groups do not guarantee equal use or human-interpretable groups.
Vocabulary growth expands label rows without changing the group count. Each
known label stores one trainable logit per group, so storage grows with both
the vocabulary size and `n_groups`.

## Learning and inspection

The training process binds batch-local label dictionaries before forward.
Growth preserves existing IDs, learned assignment rows, exposure counters, and
supported optimizer state, including the shared unavailable assignment.

When a Group is visible as an input, a downstream objective can train its
assignment logits. The forward pass selects one group, while training uses a
straight-through softmax to pass gradients to those logits. Masking the Group
as a reconstruction target trains only its state classification; it does not
train group or label reconstruction.

Vocabulary routing metrics are logged at the end of each training batch,
whether the field is an input or a reconstruction target. Each known vocabulary
entry contributes once to its argmax group; unused capacity and the unavailable
assignment are excluded. All configured groups, including unused groups, are
included in the distribution.

| Metric | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `train.vocabulary.imbalance` | `1 - min(p) / max(p)`, where `p` is the proportion of known entries routed to each group. Zero means equal routing; one means at least one group is unused. |
| `train.vocabulary.majority_class` | The largest group proportion, `max(p)`. |
| `train.vocabulary.standard_deviation` | Population standard deviation of the group proportions. |

These metrics describe the current vocabulary assignments, not label frequency
in the batch. Empty vocabularies emit no routing metrics. Validation, test, and
prediction do not emit them, and they are not averaged across the training epoch.
External loggers retain the Trainer's `log_every_n_steps` cadence; set it to `1`
to record every training step.

For an application-supplied trained `model`:

```python
labels = rf.Group.vocabulary(model, rf.Address("merchant"))
assignments = rf.Group.assignments(model, rf.Address("merchant"))
```

`labels` is an index-ordered tuple. Each assignment contains a group ID and
probabilities across all configured columns. These inspection calls read local
model state under DDP.

An idle model also supports `rf.Group.assign(model, address, label, assignment)`
for persistent changes and `rf.Group.override(model, address, assignments)`
as a temporary context manager. An assignment is an integer group ID from zero
to `n_groups - 1`. These imperative APIs
grow per-label storage before writing when necessary, preserving earlier rows,
the unavailable assignment, and group width. They cannot run while the model
is active or vocabulary state is shared with workers. Overrides restore labels
and assignments on exit; any expanded allocation remains available. Saving or
rebuilding during an open override is rejected.

## Prediction

For a decoded Group target, `group` contains the decoder's best group integer
`value` and softmax `probability`. The Group objective does not train this
decoder's group head, so that output is not a learned identity assignment or a
calibrated confidence. No vocabulary label is decoded. Use `Group.assignments`
to inspect known input labels, and evaluate unknown-label populations separately.

See the [prediction envelope](../reference/prediction-output.qmd) for shared
state probabilities, `inferred`, and repeated shapes.

The [plain-input experiment](../evidence/group/plain-input-is-dormant.html)
tracks assignment agreement when downstream supervision is available. The
[regime recovery experiment](../evidence/group/regime-recovery.html) compares
assignments with hidden generating groups and measures predictions for new
observations of known identities, against a no-regime control. Consult the
selected run and its criteria for results; older Cluster measurements do not
validate this Group implementation.
